subject: Request: carve out for customer-run NAT handlers & latency attribution
messages:
From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra@lumenwave.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Carve-out request: our NAT/edge boxes impacting latency attribution

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Quick follow-up: LumenWave runs stateful NAT/load-balancer appliances inside our VPC that terminate client TCP sessions before traffic reaches Redwood’s private deployment. On a recent spike we saw token-generation latencies climb and our ops team traced the tail back to those appliances (NAT table churn + asymmetric routing).

Given we control those appliances, we need two things from Redwood to proceed with Dedicated/private deployment:

- A written carve-out in the SLA that attributes latency and availability impacts caused by customer-managed edge appliances to the customer.
- A minimal evidence protocol so we can pass network diagnostics (pcap snippets, traceroutes, NAT table dumps) during audits without exposing full traffic.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to bill these incidents as customer-side and what evidence you require? We also want to minimize any billing or credit negotiations during onboarding.

Best,
Alejandra Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure
LumenWave Therapeutics

Attachment: network-diagnostic-summary.pdf (3 pages, redacted traces)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra@lumenwave.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Carve-out request: our NAT/edge boxes impacting latency attribution

Hi Alejandra — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Appreciate the directness; this is exactly the sort of operational split we need to nail at contract time.

Short answers up front: yes, Redwood can accept a customer-controlled-infra carve-out for latency and availability attribution for Private/VPC deployments, subject to:

1) A narrowly scoped appendix to the SLA that enumerates the exact components and failure modes that are excluded (e.g., customer-managed NAT, third-party SD-WAN appliances, and on-prem transit gateways).

2) An evidence protocol that balances forensic value with data minimization — we prefer redacted pcaps + signed attestations plus traceroutes and timing samples.

3) An operational runbook that defines escalation flow and a 72-hour joint-debug window before credit calculations.

I'm looping in Karthik (solutions) and Kimberly (sales/legal touch) to scope the appendix language and the practical steps for evidence exchange. Can you confirm LumenWave's preferred retention window for diagnostic artifacts and whether you can provide time-sliced TCP-level dumps (e.g., 30s samples) rather than long pcaps?

Next step: we'll draft proposed appendix language and a short runbook template for your ops team to review.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions - Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-sla-appendix-lumenwave.docx (draft)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra@lumenwave.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out request: our NAT/edge boxes impacting latency attribution

Alejandra — quick technical notes from our ops side so the appendix can be specific:

- We can exclude customer-run NAT/load-balancer appliances from latency SLO computations if the appendix lists the devices by function and their IP ranges. Generic language is risky; enumerate.

- Evidence we need (min set): synchronized timestamps (NTP-synced), a 30–60s packet capture (redacted headers allowed), a traceroute from the customer ingress to the Redwood private endpoint, and a brief manifest of configuration changes in the preceding 24 hours.

- For privacy/regulatory reasons, we accept redacted pcaps where payloads are removed and only headers & timing remain. Hashes of full pcaps may be supplied to prove integrity without sharing payloads.

- Important: if the customer-run appliance performs TLS termination, we cannot rely on header-only pcaps for request attribution; in those cases we need signed application-level logs (request id, timestamp, http path) to reconcile token vs. network tails.

Operational ask: can LumenWave commit to NTP across the flow and to a grouped contact list for the 72-hour debug window? We'll include a template runbook in the appendix draft.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out request: our NAT/edge boxes impacting latency attribution — legal/controls note

Folks — from the controls/compliance side a couple of constraints we should bake into the appendix: 

1) The carve-out must require the customer to maintain evidence for a minimum of 90 days and to provide evidence within 5 business days of a Redwood request. This avoids indefinite disputes.

2) We should include a standard binding attestation (signed by an authorized LumenWave operations lead) confirming that the devices identified are under customer control and that any configuration changes are logged.

3) For any incident that could impact Redwood's SOC2 evidence, we reserve the right to perform an independent audit of the relevant network-handling processes subject to reasonable notice and scoping. We can negotiate audit windows, but the right should remain.

4) We should define a clear scope for audit access, data handling, and allowed evidence formats/procedures so both parties understand limits and expectations.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Controls & Compliance
